set.body:
Source: 2026-07-25 review finding 2.

Problem:
LocalLogReader.fileIdentity (local/LocalLogReader.scala:150-158) digests path|fileKey|creationTime. On Linux, sun.nio.fs.UnixFileAttributes.creationTime() falls back to lastModifiedTime() because birthtimeSupported() is Darwin-only. Appending to a live log therefore changes the identity, the next read hits the mismatch branch (:121) and returns CursorInvalid, and follow (:70) treats CursorInvalid as terminal. Live log following is broken on the deployment platform.

Why tests miss it:
macOS/APFS has a real birthtime, so the identity is stable locally (verified). No test appends between two reads: LocalLogReaderSuite writes the file whole then reads twice, and the truncation test passes for the wrong reason on Linux. CI is ubuntu-22.04 and still green.

Acceptance:
- Identity material excludes creationTime; fileKey (dev,ino) plus path is sufficient and stable.
- Rotation/truncation still invalidate the cursor (size regression and fileKey change).
- A regression test reads a page, appends, reads again, and asserts a Page rather than CursorInvalid.
- A follow test observes at least two pages across an append.
set.title: P6f.29: Make local log file identity stable across appends on Linux
